hook: Built beside the California Brewing Company for one of its partners, and left facing Market Street once the brewery came down.

narrative.lead: The lots immediately north held the California Brewing Company's plant from 1892 until 1915, when the city bought their Douglass Street frontage for the Market Street extension. A service station stood on what was left of the ground from 1932 until it was demolished in 1980, and condominiums took the site in 1982.

building.completed_conflict: The assessor's roll gives 1895; a water-service record and an April 1896 directory listing date completion to October 1896.

historical_record.description: Water service was connected on 24 August 1896, while the house was going up.
Completed in October 1896, a Beaux Arts house built for Henry Peters (1858–1930), one of the four partners in the California Brewing Company next door.

The brewery next door came down after the city bought its Douglass Street frontage for the Market Street extension — $80,000 to the company and $69,000 to the owner of this house, recorded on 15 September 1915.

unknowns: The assessor's roll dates the building to 1895; a water-service record of August 1896 and a directory listing of April 1896 put its completion in October 1896. Neither year has been checked against a building permit.
